Date: 2028-04-09T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: Model Omega v3 — P95 latency step-up (us-east)

Hi Dylan,

Quick heads up: starting at ~07:50 ET our production telemetry shows P95 for requests backed by Model Omega v3 (seq len ~1024) in us-east jumping from ~230ms to ~690ms across multiple routes. This started after the v3 rollout at 06:00 ET. No config changes on our side.

Attached is the P95 chart for the last 3 hours (p95_graph.png). We're seeing a clear step and an increase in CPU and GPU latency on our side as well. Impact: a subset of user flows (search & summarization) are timing out intermittently which is affecting user sessions.

Ask: can Redwood either:
- Immediately route affected traffic to v2 (canary) while you investigate, or
- Approve a short SLA carveout/window while you patch the regression and roll a fix?

We are ready to accept a temporary fallback if that speeds mitigation. Please advise next steps and whether you need additional logs from our side.

Thanks,
Carlos
Senior Platform Engineer
Lumos.ai

On Mon, Apr 9, 2028 at 08:21 Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rishi / SRE: can you triage...

Quick summary from an initial pass:
- We reproduced the P95 jump in us-east for Omega v3.
- Root cause hypothesis: a change in v3's generation loop increases average KV-cache footprint for long sequences, triggering slower memory paths on the current kernel at scale.
- Evidence: concurrent increase in GPU mem utilisation and GC-like stalls correlating with request spikes; heap dumps attached (heap_dumps.tar).

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Canary rollback: shift 60% of traffic for affected routes in us-east back to Omega v2 for a 6-hour window while we patch v3 kernel path. Low-risk, immediate.
2) Traffic shaping: cap max inflight for v3 in us-east to reduce pressure; preserves some v3 traffic.
3) Fast patch: apply kernel-level workarounds (takes ~4-8 hours with risk on edge cases).

Recommendation: initiate option 1 (canary rollback to v2 for us-east) and open SRE-4982 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4982) to track remediation. We need leadership sign-off for an SLA carveout window to avoid automatic SLA credits while rollback completes.

Rishi
Sr. SRE Manager
Redwood Inference
